name: nginx.source.nginx_org
description: Move nginx from Ondřej Surý's ondrej/nginx PPA, which Launchpad removed, to nginx.org's mainline packages, on Ubuntu 22.04 or later. It refuses unless the installed nginx is the PPA's build (its version has deb.sury.org) and nginx -t passes. It backs up everything it touches under /var/backups/nginx-source, then: removes the load_module lines for modules nginx.org doesn't ship (brotli, geoip, image-filter, xslt, ssl-ct) from nginx.conf and modules-enabled, and runs nginx -t with the current nginx; removes /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ondrej-ubuntu-nginx-* (and any other sources file naming the PPA); installs nginx.org's signing key (compiled into the agent) to /usr/share/keyrings/nginx-archive-keyring.gpg, its mainline source and a pin (Pin: origin nginx.org, Pin: release o=nginx, priority 900) in /etc/apt/preferences.d/99nginx; refreshes nginx.org's list only and simulates the upgrade. If any of that fails, every file is put back and nothing else changes. Then apt-get install --only-upgrade -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold nginx, removing modules-enabled links the upgrade left dangling, nginx -t and a restart. It warns when nginx.org's conf.d/default.conf has become a port's default server. The PPA's package can't be reinstalled afterwards. The dry run (and the nginx_source state tool) lists what will change.
health_check: The helper checks that dpkg reports nginx.org's build, nginx -t passes and nginx restarted.
